notes: Delegation journeys across both KAS subagent tools: orchestrate_subagent crews (parallel, dependent, failure) and single invoke_sub_agent delegations (approve, deny, coalesced parallel).

scenarios.name: Delegate a task to a blocking subagent
scenarios.description: User asks the agent to use a subagent for a task; the crew is orchestrated, the subagent runs to completion, and the main agent reports back — the basic delegate-and-wait workflow
steps: prompt:use a subagent to summarize the README
scenarios.observe: The orchestration card shows the crew running then completing; the roster lists the delegated agent reaching a terminal Completed state; the main agent synthesizes a final answer once the pipeline returns.

scenarios.name: Orchestrate a multi-stage research pipeline
scenarios.description: User asks the agent to research two areas with a two-stage crew; the agent orchestrates it and synthesizes both results into the main thread once the pipeline completes. End-state asserts the orchestrate card + synthesis (the collapsed card does not expose per-stage parallelism, which is exercised in the fixture but not asserted)
steps: prompt:research the auth and storage modules in parallel using subagents
scenarios.observe: A multi-stage crew orchestrates; each stage runs as its own agent and reaches a terminal state; the main agent produces one synthesized summary after the whole pipeline returns, and per-stage output does not leak into the main transcript mid-run.

scenarios.name: Delegate to a single subagent and approve it
scenarios.description: User delegates one task to a single subagent (KAS invoke_sub_agent — the top-level delegation tool in cloud sandboxes, distinct from the multi-stage orchestrate crew); the subagent approval gate appears, the user approves, the delegation runs through the invoke pipeline adapter, and the main agent reports back — the single-delegation subagent workflow
steps: prompt:delegate a single subagent to summarize the readme
scenarios.observe: The single-delegation invoke_sub_agent call surfaces a subagent approval gate; approving it runs the delegation through the invoke pipeline adapter (rendered as a normalized Orchestrated card), and the main agent synthesizes after the subagent thread returns. Requires the cloud-parity adapter, enabled here via env. The synthesis turn matches on the subagent's own returned text rather than on hasToolResults, which the fake KRS implements as a bare emptiness check that ignores status -- an error result is still a result, so hasToolResults would fire on a failed delegation exactly as on a successful one. Matching the returned text instead means the synthesis reply cannot render unless the subagent actually ran and its output propagated back into the parent request; a delegation that failed to resolve leaves the turn unconsumed and fails the scenario.

match.userInputContains: delegate a single subagent to summarize the readme

events.name: invoke_sub_agent
events.input: {"name":"test_subagent","prompt":"Summarize the README in one line.","explanation":"summarize the readme"}

events.content: Single delegation complete: the subagent thread returned to me.

scenarios.name: Deny a single subagent delegation
scenarios.description: User delegates a task to a single subagent (invoke_sub_agent); the subagent approval gate appears, the user denies it, the delegation reaches a terminal Rejected state without running, and the main agent acknowledges and adapts — the deny-and-recover subagent workflow
steps: prompt:delegate a single subagent for the risky task
verify: screen.contains:Understood, I will not run that delegation
scenarios.observe: The single-delegation invoke_sub_agent call surfaces a subagent approval gate; denying it drives the delegation to a terminal Rejected state without running, and the main agent acknowledges and continues. Requires the cloud-parity adapter, enabled here via env.

match.userInputContains: delegate a single subagent for the risky task

events.content: Understood, I will not run that delegation.

scenarios.name: Parallel single subagents coalesce into one card
scenarios.description: User asks for two subagents in parallel; KAS emits two separate invoke_sub_agent calls, each gated for approval, and the invoke pipeline adapter coalesces them into ONE Orchestrating card with a two-stage roster (auth, storage) rather than two stacked single-agent cards — the parallel single-delegation workflow
verify: screen.contains:Both delegations returned to the main thread
scenarios.observe: Two invoke_sub_agent calls each surface a subagent approval gate; once approved, the pipeline adapter coalesces them into a single Orchestrated (2 agents) card (not two stacked cards), and the main agent synthesizes one answer after both delegations return. Requires the cloud-parity adapter, enabled here via env. The synthesis turn matches on the subagent's own returned text rather than on hasToolResults, so the reply cannot render unless a delegation actually ran and returned; hasToolResults would fire on an error result too, since the fake KRS only checks that the result array is non-empty.

events.content: Both delegations returned to the main thread.
